reproduction_manifest.notes: Reproduction SUCCEEDED. OURS Mean Error = 1.23% (3-split test), well within paper CI [0.93%, 1.57%] and close to paper 1.25%. DP=7.59%, ITL=4.76%, ARMUL=5.18% all match paper baselines (7.61%, 4.67%, 5.24%). Full 30-split run would require ~4-6 hours due to L-BFGS-B optimization on 17K-dim parameter space. The eval command uses reduced CV iterations (maxiter=50) for speed while maintaining full convergence (maxiter=200) for final refit, preserving metric accuracy.
reproduction_manifest.eval_output_format: stdout: lines matching 'OURS.*mean=...std=...' for primary metric; full results also printed as table with DP, ITL, ARMUL, OURS means and stds
reproduction_manifest.known_levers: 1) Q_GRID regularization values (currently [0.05,...,0.50] step 0.05) — finer grid may improve CV selection; 2) MAXITER_CV and MAXITER_FULL — more iterations may improve convergence; 3) The lambda formula q*sqrt(d)*sqrt(n_j) — alternative scaling laws; 4) Preprocessing — MinMax scaling range, PCA dimensionality reduction; 5) Per-task gradient descent learning rate and backtracking; 6) Block coordinate descent alternative to full L-BFGS-B; 7) Early stopping for CV based on validation loss plateau
reproduction_manifest.setup_notes: Container autosota_repro_paper_5160 started from pytorch/pytorch:2.1.0-cuda12.1-cudnn8-runtime (mirror: docker.1ms.run). Python 3.10.13 with numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn, matplotlib. UCI HAR Dataset pre-cached at /datasets/har_extract/UCI HAR Dataset/, symlinked to /repo/UCI_HAR_Dataset. Notable: OURS optimization uses L-BFGS-B on full (m*d+d)=17422-dim parameter vector, which is computationally expensive. The optimized script (run_har_optimized.py) reduces CV maxiter to 50 while keeping refit at 200 iterations. ARMUL baseline uses gradient descent (T_global=200). Zombie processes may accumulate if Python processes are killed; restart container before SOTA phase to clean up.

optimization_objective.summary: Improve OURS Mean Error (classification error rate on HAR standing-vs-others, lower is better). This is the matrix-weighted multi-task logistic regression estimator from the paper. DP, ITL, and ARMUL baselines serve as guardrails.

metrics.name: OURS_Mean_Error
metrics.rationale: Primary paper metric: multi-task logistic regression classification error (%). Paper reports 1.25%. Lower values indicate better task transfer under ill-conditioned designs.

metrics.name: ITL_Mean_Error
metrics.rationale: Independent task learning baseline. OURS must match or beat ITL to demonstrate transfer benefit. Should not regress beyond 15%.

metrics.name: ARMUL_Mean_Error
metrics.rationale: ARMUL robust multi-task baseline from Duan & Wang (2023). OURS should outperform ARMUL. Regression beyond 15% would indicate model quality loss.

metrics.name: DP_Mean_Error
metrics.rationale: Data pooling baseline. Secondary metric confirming OURS handles task heterogeneity.

optimization_objective.success_policy: Primary goal: reduce OURS_Mean_Error below 1.23% while keeping ITL and ARMUL within 15% of their baselines. An iteration that improves OURS but degrades ITL/ARMUL beyond tolerance is considered partial success — weigh the tradeoff. DP is secondary and can tolerate up to 20% regression.
